questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 14 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area of a triangle is ½ × base × height, so ½ × 14 × 6 = 42 cm². Slow down and halve before multiplying, don't just multiply base by height.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14)

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: Total surface area = 2πrh + 2πr² = (2×3.14×3×5) + (2×3.14×9) = 94.2 + 56.5 = 150.7 cm². The distractors come from forgetting one of the two parts or adding them wrongly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a reaction, what do we call the starting substances before they react?
questions.why: The reactants are the starting substances; their total mass equals the total mass of the products formed in a closed system.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call it when a chemical reaction releases heat and feels warm?
questions.why: An exothermic reaction releases heat energy to its surroundings, which is why it feels warm to touch.
